title: observability: propagate request_id & trace context across API surface; add per-endpoint metrics tags
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Improve observability and debuggability across the API surface (hosted API, OpenAI compatibility layer, and streaming) by consistently propagating request IDs and trace context, emitting structured logs with fields developers expect, and tagging per-endpoint metrics so cost/latency breakdowns are attributable at the route level. This change also fixes several streaming edge-cases where the request id was dropped for streaming reconnects and ensures tool/function-calling flows carry the same trace metadata. What I changed: - Introduced a per-request Request-ID generator/propagator that respects incoming X-Request-Id or generates a stable id when missing. - Plumbed traceparent and tracestate headers through the API gateway, openai-compat shim, and serving runtime adapter so distributed traces stitch end-to-end. - Standardized structured log schema for API entry/exit, stream events, tool invocation start/finish, and function/tool-calling errors. Logs include: request_id, trace_id, span_id, route, route_version, user_id (when present), client_type, and sampling flag. - Added per-endpoint metric tags in the metrics shim (route, model_family, compatibility_mode=openai|redwood) so Grafana dashboards and per-route SLOs can be computed without aggregation hacks. - Streaming stability fixes: keep request_id and parent trace headers during reconnect/resume flow; add guard to avoid double-ending a stream if runtime sends duplicate EOS. - OpenAI-compat updates: ensure compat layer mirrors X-Request-Id -> request_id, and maps OpenAI-style 'response' events into structured logs while preserving trace headers. - Tests: unit tests for propagators, integration test that runs through gateway -> openai-compat -> runtime with traces preserved, and an e2e streaming test that asserts single request_id across resume. Backwards compatibility: headers are optional (fields are additive). No behavioral changes to user-facing payloads other than stronger logs/metrics. Checklist: - [x] Request-id generator and propagation implemented - [x] Traceparent/tracestate plumbing + tests - [x] Structured log schema defined and implemented - [x] Per-endpoint metric tags added - [x] Streaming reconnect stability fixes - [x] OpenAI compat layer mapping updated - [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests updated - [x] Docs snippet updated in redwood-docs (link in files) Related: ENG-2315 (observability roadmap), ENG-2450 (streaming reliability).
commits: feat(observability): add request-id propagator across gateway and compat layer
fix(streaming): preserve request_id and trace headers on reconnect
chore(test): add e2e streaming trace-preservation test
docs: add observability notes for request-id and per-route metrics
review_comments: Marco Chen: Can you confirm that we never reuse generated request ids across retries? If a client retries a request, how do we detect it?

Aisha Patel (reply): We generate a stable id per incoming connection/request. Retries that come with the same X-Request-Id will be correlated by the caller. We also attach an internal attempt counter on logs for retries so events for the same request are easily grouped.
Olivia Ruiz: The structured log schema looks good. Please add a brief example JSON in the docs showing a streaming 'response' event with request_id + traceparent.
Aisha Patel (reply): Added example in redwood-docs; also included the mapping in openai-compat tests.
Samir Khatri: Metrics tags are great. Please ensure metric cardinality is bounded for model_version and route_version — we should tag only model_family and leave model_version out by default.

Aisha Patel (reply): Agree; changed tags to include model_family and route_version only when explicitly configured. Added a config flag metrics.include_route_version (default false) documented in redwood-docs.
Hannah Lee: CI flaky on first run due to ordering; reran and all green. Left one minor nits comment inline.
Aisha Patel (reply): Addressed nit and pushed squash commit.
release_notes: Added consistent request_id and trace propagation across API gateway, openai-compat layer, and runtime adapter; structured logging schema for API events; per-endpoint metric tags to enable per-route cost/latency dashboards; streaming stability fixes for reconnect/resume.
notes_for_release: No breaking API changes. Ops: update tracing sampler settings if you want traces for ingress-only flows. Dashboards updated under Observability -> API Routes.
